title: Super Agents and Confounders: Influence of surrounding agents on vehicle trajectory prediction
abstract: arXiv:2604.03463v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: In highly interactive driving scenes, trajectory prediction is conditioned on information from surrounding traffic participants such as cars and pedestrians. Our main contribution is a comprehensive analysis of state-of-the-art trajectory predictors, which reveals a surprising and critical flaw: many surrounding agents degrade prediction accuracy rather than improve it. Using Shapley-based attribution, we rigorously demonstrate that models learn unstable and non-causal decision-making schemes that vary significantly across training runs. Building on these insights, we propose to integrate a Conditional Information Bottleneck (CIB), which does not require additional supervision and is trained to effectively compress agent features as well as ignore those that are not beneficial for the prediction task. translated_title: 超级智能体与混淆因素：周围智能体对车辆轨迹预测的影响
translated_abstract: 在高度交互的驾驶场景中，轨迹预测依赖于周围交通参与者（如汽车和行人）的信息。我们的主要贡献是对最先进的轨迹预测器进行了全面分析，揭示了一个令人惊讶且关键的缺陷：许多周围智能体会降低而非提高预测精度。借助基于Shapley值的归因方法，我们严格证明了模型学习到的是不稳定的、非因果的决策方案，且这些方案在不同的训练运行之间存在显著差异。基于这些发现，我们提出引入条件信息瓶颈（Conditional Information Bottleneck, CIB），该方法无需额外的监督信息，通过训练有效压缩智能体特征，并忽略那些对预测任务无益的特征。在多个数据集和模型架构上进行的全面实验表明，这种简单而有效的方法不仅能……
tldr: 该论文发现周围智能体信息反而会降低轨迹预测的精度，并提出无需额外监督的条件信息瓶颈（CIB）方法，通过压缩有效特征、过滤无益信息来提升预测性能的稳定性与因果性。
en_tdlr: This paper reveals that surrounding agents can degrade rather than improve trajectory prediction accuracy, and proposes a supervision-free Conditional Information Bottleneck (CIB) that compresses beneficial agent features while ignoring unhelpful ones to enhance prediction performance.
